statement: The batch-1 seat-2 constant-last-place anomaly (mean_rank 4.0 in all 16 games) is caused by duel-hardcoded doctrine geometry (march target (-4,3) sitting beside seat-2 territory), not by doctrine quality.
prediction: After the geometry seam (3015cb4), the same 16-game baseline shows seat-2 mean_rank < 3.5 (was 4.0) and seat spread across seats shrinks.

outcome.secondary: with the seat confound removed the doctrine gap widened: turtler mean_rank 1.75 (14 wins) vs expansionist 3.25 (2 wins); pre-seam 2.31 vs 2.66
outcome.residual: seat2 remains mildly elevated (2.875 vs ~2.37 pooled elsewhere) - n=16, descriptive only; candidate for a later paired test if it persists across rosters

statement: settler_broker loses because of a self-inflicted purchase-gate interaction, not income: the gate (scripted.py, turn%3==0, gold>=120) fires while SETTLER (160 gold) is unaffordable, and the next preference GRANARY (exactly 120) spends the settler bank before it can ever reach 160 on a gate turn.
prediction: If the purchase step holds gold below a bank floor until the top purchase preference is affordable (bank_floor=160 for settler_broker), it founds >=3 cities by turn 25 in the large majority of games and mean_rank improves by >=0.5; granary purchases drop to near zero.

test.param: purchase bank floor (scripted.py gate, needs a doctrine-level opt-in field)

evidence: batch-002 trajectories: cities flat at 2 in every inspected match while gold sawtooths 38-173 and CLEARS 160 between gate turns (t=25: 162, t=35: 173 in batch-002-s300003-r2); drops of ~110-120 gold right after gate turns match GRANARY purchases exactly (rules.py purchase_cost = 2x production: SETTLER 160, GRANARY 120)
